findings.title: The chapter's footing query and the physical body disagree by exactly one voxel cell at the Origin audit site, so the survey can never start
findings.statement: In a 189.8 s hardware run of ?story=ch13-survey the body reached S and 200 F attempts on the shipped resolver (interactionId story-ch13-survey-start, source resolver-perform, performOutcome returned each time) left survey.phase at 'awaiting-start' with 0 samples and the prompt permanently live. The chapter's own diagnostic reports supported=false at the grounded body pose for 1501 of 1555 world-bound samples. The only other gate on commitCommonGroundSurveyStart (commonGroundDirector.ts:1069-1076) is CG_POINT_REACH 2.0, satisfied at 0.310 units, so the refusal is the footing predicate. A bounded height-response diagnostic then measured WHY the query disagrees: see heightResponseMeasured.

measured.supportedTrueObservedAt: bodyPose [6.836,51.186,-6.0] near the landed ship, rail 'walk'
measured.supportedFalseFrom: bodyPose [-29.083,50.99,-1.133] onward, i.e. the whole approach to and area around the audit site

sourceCandidatesNotConfirmed: main/src/story/world/CommonGroundWorld.tsx createFooting/supportedColumn: the support cell is ASSUMED to be exactly cell(y-1.05) with cell+1 required empty, where cell(v)=Math.round(v/VOXEL_SCALE) and VOXEL_SCALE=2. The shipped agent navigation (src/utils/agentSurfaceNavigation.ts:353-360) instead SEARCHES DOWNWARD for the first solid cell whose outward neighbour is empty. A single assumed cell, a logical/rendered disagreement, or the water/hazard clauses could each produce this.

The same file's five-point disc sample (centre and +/-0.5 in x and z) is degenerate at VOXEL_SCALE 2: all five offsets round to the SAME voxel cell, so the stated 'a foot half over a hole' protection is not actually exercised. Observation, not the cause.

createLiveAgentSurfaceTerrain isSolidVoxel mixes voxelSystem.hasVoxel with generator.shouldVoxelExist && !isDeleted; a generated-vs-rendered/WorldSave disagreement at the audit site would show exactly this shape.

The FAILING CLAUSE remains inferred, not read: 'solid(cy) false' cannot be separated from 'solid(cy+1) true' by an outside observer. The lift-to-26 TRUE result requires solid(26) AND air(27), which is what makes the one-cell disagreement the reading the measurement supports.

findings.statement: Independent correction to root's 10:02 note: the empty anchorLedger in home-movie-2 is NOT missing instrumentation. Anchor capture works — survey-movie-1 recorded anc.cg.repeated-measure (sequence 1) with its exact signed event text and the worker pose. In home-movie-2 the loop exited on its --until-beat predicate at 2777 ms and anc.cg.hatch-boarded activated afterwards, appearing only in the post-loop finalState sample. Separately, no ch13-home anchor activated during that deep-linked run: anc.cg.cell-installed is signed as 'the actual live install receipt from the prior station-continuation contract', which a deep link cannot produce, and signedSceneAvRuntime.activateAnchor refuses an anchor while an earlier pending ordered anchor of the same beat is unactivated. The four ch13-home anchors are therefore expected to be observable only in the continuous station->home journey, which is exactly where they must be proven.
findings.revisionReason: Score's home-anchor eligibility interpretation (score-home-anchor-eligibility-interpretation.md) explicitly rejects the 'all four home anchors are continuous-journey-only' reading, and I accept that correction.
findings.statementRevised: Two separable observations, restated. (1) Anchor instrumentation is sound: the survey runs recorded anc.cg.repeated-measure and anc.cg.demonstration-opened with exact signed ids/events, and home-movie-2's empty ledger is a capture-window artefact — the loop exited on its --until-beat predicate at 2777 ms and anc.cg.hatch-boarded activated afterwards, surviving only in the post-loop finalState. (2) I withdraw my earlier inference that ALL FOUR ch13-home anchors are provable only in a continuous journey. Per Score's binding reading, only anc.cg.cell-installed requires the live install boundary; anc.cg.home-steady must restore silently on a hydrated entry, and anc.cg.fault-reviewed / anc.cg.return-chosen bind to the actual F acts, which DID occur in home-movie-2 through the shared resolver. On that reading, the observed absence of home-steady, fault-reviewed and return-chosen during a valid deep link is an OPEN ANOMALY, not expected behaviour.
findings.openAnomaly: Deep-linked ch13-home performed both real F acts (interactionTrace resolver-perform, milestones ch13FaultReviewed and ch13ReturnChosen set, beat advanced) yet activationHistoryAnchorIds stayed empty for the whole in-loop window. Source risk candidates, read-only and unconfirmed, matching Score's own reading: noteAnchor() latches runtime.firedAnchors BEFORE calling activateSignedSceneAnchorById and discards its boolean result, so a rejected activation is still spent locally and can never retry; and activateAnchor() refuses any anchor while an earlier pending ordered same-beat anchor (here cell-installed, unobtainable on a deep link) is unactivated. Together these could permanently suppress the later, eligible home anchors. NOT PROVEN: I did not instrument activateAnchor's return value, and I make no audibility claim — Score correctly notes local score dispatch may continue despite a rejected AV activation, and nothing was listened to.

The captured frame 0039-root-checkpoint.png shows the view from INSIDE the cockpit (yoke, throttle, canopy frame) with the debug HUD reading 'Ship: landed' and 'Flight: surface / flight'.

In a continuous journey ch13-return performs exit-ship before advancing, so this may be confined to direct beat entry — that is NOT yet measured and must be confirmed by the continuous run.

It is DISTINCT from CG-IMPL-004 (interaction cadence) and CG-IMPL-005 (waypoint retargeting): no route progress algorithm was reached at all, because the body never left the ship. findings.category: movie-rail arrival predicate vs live body height
findings.statement: On the repaired build, the ch13 movie rail can never begin the survey recording, because its arrival gates compare a FULL 3D distance between the player's live world position and poses authored on the ground plane. Measured: the player's body y is 52.79-52.80 in every one of 2643 samples while CG_POSES.S is authored at y = 51.05, so the minimum achievable 3D distance to S is 1.745 units (horizontal 0.13). The rail's gate is CG_RAIL_START_AIM + CG_RAIL_ROUTE_ARRIVE = 0.35 + 0.35 = 0.70, which the body can never satisfy. Terra therefore walked 58.6 real units to the survey start, stood within 0.5 horizontal units of it for 261 of 354 pose-ledger entries (~4.5 minutes) with routeAction 'walk' and the live prompt '[F] Begin recording your route', and never acted. The frame 0038-strip-ch13-survey.png shows the marker reading 'survey start · begin a route · 0m' with the F prompt on screen and 'Flight: surface / fps'.
findings.whyTheResolverStillOffersIt: The shipped resolver reach is CG_POINT_REACH = 2.0, which 1.745 satisfies with only 0.255 units of margin. That is why the player-facing prompt appears while the rail's tighter gate cannot close.
findings.whyTheTestsMissedIt: main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.test.ts standAt() calls setPlayerWorldPosition(point.x, point.y, point.z) with the authored pose y (51.05) — a body of zero height. Every rail regression therefore runs at a vertical offset of 0, and the 3026 passing tests cannot see this seam.
findings.impactOnVerification: BLOCKING for the remaining commission. The 18-unit common span, both route classes, the long-vs-short route classes, the three cold focused journeys, the station->home->ch13 continuation and the ch13 segment of the full story movie all sit downstream of an act the rail cannot perform. The CG-IMPL-005 ordered-cursor repair is consequently STILL UNTESTED in a browser: no route traversal was ever entered.
findings.notDone: No source edit, no threshold change, no teleport, no progress grant, no rescue. Radii and predicates are the integrator's to change, not the verifier's.
findings.reconciliation: Root correctly asked me to reconcile the actual body frame before calling this a threshold problem. Doing so SHARPENS the finding rather than dissolving it. getPlayerWorldPosition() returns the Rapier capsule CENTRE (EfficientPlayer CapsuleCollider args [PLAYER_CAPSULE_HALF_HEIGHT 1.3, PLAYER_CAPSULE_RADIUS 0.5]; EfficientPlayer.tsx:1525 itself derives feet as centre - HALF_HEIGHT). Feet therefore sit centre - (1.3 + 0.5) = centre - 1.8. Measured body centre y 52.79 -> feet y 50.99, against the authored S plane y 51.05: her FEET are within 0.06 units of the authored ground plane and 0.13 units horizontally of S. Distance from the FEET to S is 0.143 units, which passes the 0.70 gate comfortably. The gate fails only because the comparison is made from the capsule centre in full 3D. So this is a COORDINATE-FRAME mismatch (centre-vs-feet / vertical inclusion) in the rail's arrival comparison, not a too-tight radius and not a body that failed to arrive. She is physically standing on the mark — the HUD marker itself prints '0m'.
findings.candidateFixSpace: Reconciling the comparison frame (feet or ground-projected) is the integrator's decision; widening radii would mask it and could relax genuine physical clearance rules. No prescription is made here.
sourceCitations: main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.test.ts:99 (standAt places the body AT the authored pose y — a zero-height body, which is why 3026 tests pass)
